tech_ai_semis.rationale: Facts: after Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the Nov 3 midterms, prominent Democrats called for limits on AI data centers (including a 'national data center moratorium'), and on Nov 5 the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell more than 12% (Nvidia -9.3%, AMD -17.3%, Micron -17.5%, Broadcom -10.4%); XLK fell 8% on the week, its worst since April 2025. Bloomberg/CNBC report Microsoft is winding down its Oracle capacity deal and trimming its neocloud partners, with some GPU contracts pushed into 1H27. Offsetting fundamentals are strong: AMD posted record Q3 revenue of $13.4B with data center up 97% and guided Q4 to about $17B, and Apple reported record September-quarter iPhone revenue. Interpretation: earnings are holding up, but policy risk to the US data center buildout, signs of hyperscaler capacity discipline and a market pricing about 70% odds of a December Fed hike point to lower multiples and a mild headwind. The risk is skewed to the downside, and Nvidia's Nov 17 report is the key swing factor; this is not yet a -2 because no law or rule has changed and analysts doubt legislation can stall construction (any bill needs the President's signature).

us_large_broad.rationale: Facts: the S&P 500 fell 4.4% on Nov 5, with all 11 sectors lower. It was the index's worst day since April 2025, and the Magnificent Seven lost more than $1 trillion in combined market value. The S&P ended the week down 2.7% and the Nasdaq entered correction territory. October payrolls rose 165,000 against roughly 59,000-65,000 expected, and markets priced about a 70% chance of a December Fed hike. Interpretation: the earnings base is intact (Apple record quarter, Palantir beat-and-raise), and Bank of America frames the selloff as multiple compression rather than estimate cuts. But the index's heavy tech/AI weight, a new policy overhang on the AI capex cycle and rising rate-hike risk make the next 1-3 months a mild headwind for cap-weighted US large caps.

regime_notes: The regime shifted this week from 'AI capex can only go up' to a political and financing-discipline test. Democrats' midterm sweep put data center restrictions on the agenda: moratorium calls, local ballot measures and Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa's call to halt data center work until protections are in place. That triggered a 12% one-day SOX drop and a Nasdaq correction. Microsoft's reported Oracle wind-down and neocloud consolidation add a second, demand-side signal: hyperscalers are rationing third-party capacity even as they keep 2026 capex at record levels (Alphabet about $195-205B, Meta $135-145B per late-October guidance). Reported fundamentals stay strong (AMD data center +97% and a $17B Q4 guide; TSMC guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B in mid-October), so the hit is to multiples, not yet to earnings. Analysts disagree: BofA says it is a valuation reset, while Yorkville's Dan Ives now sees Big Tech capex growth peaking in 2027. A strong jobs print and about 70% odds of a December Fed hike work against long-duration tech valuations. Asia's chip-heavy markets were hit too: CNBC reported that the Nikkei and Taiwan's Taiex entered bear markets and the Kospi fell more than 6%.

red_flags.target: XLK, QQQ, SMH, SOXX (tech-heavy and semiconductor ETFs)
red_flags.issue: Concentration risk has materialised. The risk sits in a single factor: AI data center capex now has political and regulatory exposure after the midterms. On Nov 5 the SOX fell more than 12% and the Magnificent Seven lost more than $1T (Nvidia alone more than $440B); XLK fell 8% on the week, its worst since April 2025. The Magnificent Seven were about 32-35% of the S&P 500 in mid/late 2026 (FinanceBuzz; secondary source). Note that index weights probably fell this week because the mega-caps dropped most, so this flag reflects concentrated, correlated drawdown risk, not a new high in weights.

Volatility regime break: SOX fell more than 12% in one session (Nov 5), then rose 4.2% on Nov 6. Expect wide intraday moves and possible bid-ask widening in leveraged semiconductor products around Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings.
Index-level concentration: the Magnificent Seven are about a third of the S&P 500 (secondary source), so 'broad' US large-cap ETFs carry a large implicit AI/semis bet.
